chunks: Abu al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Sabah al-At'tar told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin'an (meaning al-O'aqi), on the authority of Abu Jamrah, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Qays, on the authority of his father, that God's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"Whoever prays the two cool-time prayers shall enter Paradise," meaning after the morning prayer and after the afternoon prayer. The compiler of this book - may God increase his honor - said: "My intention in presenting these narrations here is to refute the opponents, because they do not consider there to be a prayer after the morning and after the afternoon prayers, so I wished to clarify that they have contradicted the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) in his saying and his action."

key_terms.الرَّدَّ عَلَى الْمُخَالِفِينَ: Refutation of the opponents, specifically those who deny the legal status of these specific prayers.
key_terms.الْبَرْدَيْنِ: The two cool-time prayers, referring to the voluntary prayers performed after the morning and afternoon prayers when the sun is less intense.
key_terms.مُصَنِّفُ هَذَا الْكِتَابِ: The compiler of the book (referring to Shaykh al-Mufid), indicating a shift from the hadith chain to the author's commentary.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'two cool-time prayers' (al-Bardayn) in Shia jurisprudence and how does this hadith refute their denial?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Khisal highlights the specific virtue of praying the 'two cool-time' prayers (al-Bardayn) after Fajr and Asr, promising Paradise to the practitioner. Shaykh al-Saduq explicitly frames this hadith as a polemical tool against jurists who deny the existence of these specific voluntary prayers, arguing that their denial contradicts both the Prophet's explicit statement and his consistent practice (Sunnah).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-108 Abul Qasim Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated that Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Tarkhan quoted Abdullah ibn al-Sabah al-At’tar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin’an, that is Al-O’aqi, on the authority of Abu Jamreh , on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Qays, on the authority of his father that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “Whoever says the two prayers at the cool times shall enter Paradise.”

This means after the morning and afternoon prayers.The compiler of the book - may God increase his honor - said, “My intention behind presenting these traditions here is to denounce those who are opposed to saying the extra prayers after the morning and afternoon prayers and that they oppose what the Prophet (MGB) said and did.”
